name: How do I compare kitchen renovation bids without getting confused by allowances?

mainEntity.name: How do I compare kitchen renovation bids without getting confused by allowances?
mainEntity.text: How do I compare kitchen renovation bids without getting confused by allowances?

acceptedAnswer.text: To compare kitchen renovation bids accurately, homeowners need to separate fixed costs from allowances. A fixed cost is a price the contractor has committed to, while an allowance is a placeholder for something not yet selected, such as cabinets, tile, plumbing fixtures, or appliances. If one bid uses very low allowances, it may appear cheaper even though the final cost will likely rise later. The best way to compare bids is to line up the same scope, same product level, and same assumptions across all proposals. Ask each contractor to show what is included, what is excluded, and what happens if the actual selection costs more than the allowance. This avoids false comparisons and surprise overruns. A detailed scope with clear allowances is far more useful than a single bottom-line number.
acceptedAnswer.description: Compare bids by separating fixed costs from allowances for items not yet selected. Check whether each allowance is realistic for cabinets, countertops, appliances, and fixtures, because low allowances make a bid look cheaper than it really is. The best comparison is an itemized scope with the same assumptions.
